To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we proposed a fast and light weight domain adaptation method for Gaussian mixture density network, which is suitable for the setting where data distribution change rapidly, and we applied it to end-to-end communication system, which can adapt to the channel changes using only a few samples.

we propose fast methods for domain adaptation of a communication auto-encoder using a very limited number of target samples, that can adapt to rapidly changing channels, and that can improve or maintain the performance of the autoencoder in the presence of changing channels.

(a) we propose a method for domain adaptation of a Gaussian mixture density model using a very small number of samples from the target domain, and (b) we propose a fast and sample-efficient method for adapting an autoencoder-based communication model under changing channel conditions, by adapting only the model of the channel, without modifying the encoder or decoder neural network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of fast adaptation of a Gaussian mixture density model (MDN) to a new data distribution using a small set of labeled samples.
the problem of domain adaptation, and more specifically the problem of fast adaptation using only a small number of samples.

the problem of adapting an MDN model using only a small number of samples from a target domain, and applying this MDN adaptation to the problem of adapting the autoencoder-based end-to-end communication system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methods for adapting an autoencoder-based end-to-end communication system can effectively compensate for the changing channel conditions, and maintain the error rate at a low value.
the proposed methods are fast, sample-efficient, and effective in adapting the MDN model and autoencoder under changing data distributions.
the proposed methods enable fast and sample-efficient domain adaptation of autoencoder-based end-to-end communication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose fast and sample-efficient domain adaptation methods for MDN and autoencoder-based end-to-end communication.
the proposed MDN and autoencoder adaptation methods are fast, light-weight, and effective for adapting to a changing channel distribution.
the proposed method is a fast and sample-efficient approach for adapting an autoencoder-based end-to-end communication system to a target channel distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fast and sample-efficient domain adaptation method can significantly improve the robustness and generalization performance of an autoencoder-based end-to-end learning system.
a small amount of adaptation can significantly improve the performance of a neural network under a changing distribution.
it is possible to adapt a communication system to changes in channel conditions without collecting a large number of labeled samples.
